summary: Sudbury District lookout in an Ontario index, with a 1937 radio installation noted. No source describes the site today.

events.note: An ultra-high frequency radio-telephone set was installed at the tower, per the Department of Lands and Forests report the index cites.

evidence.supports: 1937: radio-telephone set installed at the Secord tower, per Department of Lands and Forests report
evidence.quote: 1937: A ultra-high frequency radio-telephone set was installed at the Secord tower. (Report of the Department of Lands and Forests)

evidence.supports: Ontario towers came under the Department of Lands and Forests, which became the MNR in 1972
evidence.quote: They came under the jurisdiction of Ontario's former Department of Lands and Forests which became the Ministry of Natural Resources in 1972.

evidence.supports: Towers were used less from the 1960s as aerial spotting and firefighting took over
evidence.quote: As the 1960's progressed the towers were in use less and less as aerial fire spotting and fire fighting crews took over.

notes_for_editor: Only one source gives anything specific: the Canada Lookouts Ontario index, which lists Secord in Sudbury District and cites a 1937 Department of Lands and Forests report for the radio installation. The brief's source page, the Ontario GeoHub 'tower' dataset (https://geohub.lio.gov.on.ca/datasets/mnrf::tower), returns only a JavaScript shell to the text reader, so it is not cited. The local GeoHub export (data/raw/ontario_lio/fire_towers.geojson) lists a 'Secord Fire Tower' at 46.341509, -80.888804 with location accuracy 'Within 50 metres' and no construction date. Its quotes cannot be checked, so it is not used as evidence. The record has no local_unit; Sudbury District comes from the index and could be proposed as a local_unit after human review. Two searches found no other source on the tower's build date, staffing or fate. Story is short for that reason.
